natural: what goes around comes around

meaning.en: Heaven's justice tends to come back round: wrongdoers eventually get what they deserve.
meaning.zh: 天道循环，作恶的人终究会得到报应。

equivalents: justice catches up in the end

examples.zh: 他坑害了那么多人，最后身败名裂，真是天道好还。
examples.en: He ruined so many people and ended in disgrace: what goes around comes around.

examples.zh: 贪官落网，大家都说天道好还。
examples.en: When the corrupt official was arrested, everyone said justice had caught up with him.

usage.en: Used as a comment on someone's comeuppance, usually after the fact. Literary or formal; carries a moral, fatalistic tone.
usage.zh: 多用来评论恶人得到报应，事后感慨。书面语，带有因果报应的宿命色彩。

natural: a woman with a hero's spirit

meaning.en: A woman of admirable courage, resolve and ability, the equal of any man.
meaning.zh: 指有胆识、有气魄、有才能的女子，不亚于男子。

equivalents: a woman who stands tall among men

examples.zh: 她独自撑起家业，邻里都称她为女中丈夫。
examples.en: She single-handedly keeps the family business going, and the neighbours call her a woman of heroic mettle.

examples.zh: 这位女将军被誉为女中丈夫。
examples.en: The woman general was praised as a heroine the equal of any man.

usage.en: Praise in a traditional frame; the comparison to 'men' can sound dated today, so it is mostly literary or historical. Compare 巾帼英雄.
usage.zh: 带赞扬意味，但以“丈夫”作标准略显旧式，多见于书面或历史语境。可比较“巾帼英雄”。

natural: barely acknowledging someone

meaning.en: To treat someone coldly, half-acknowledging them as if not bothering to respond.
meaning.zh: 对人态度冷淡，爱答不理的样子。

examples.zh: 我去问价格，店员待理不理的。
examples.en: When I asked about the price the assistant barely deigned to answer.

examples.zh: 对客户待理不理，生意怎么会好？
examples.en: How can business be good if you treat customers so offhandedly?

usage.en: Describes a person's cold, lazy manner, often in service settings. Colloquial, mildly critical; usually 待理不理的.
usage.zh: 形容态度冷淡怠慢，常用于服务场合。口语，略带批评，常说“待理不理的”。

natural: set the whole world in order

meaning.en: To put the whole realm right and restore order and unity under a strong leader.
meaning.zh: 匡正天下，使天下得到安定和统一。

examples.zh: 管仲辅佐齐桓公，九合诸侯，一匡天下。
examples.en: Guan Zhong helped Duke Huan of Qi unite the lords and restore order to the realm.

examples.zh: 他有一匡天下的抱负，却生不逢时。
examples.en: He dreamed of setting the world to rights, but was born at the wrong time.

story.en: Confucius praised Guan Zhong: 'He assisted Duke Huan, made him leader of the lords, and set the whole world right' (一匡天下).
story.zh: 《论语》：“管仲相桓公，霸诸侯，一匡天下，民到于今受其赐。”

usage.en: Literary and grand in tone; used for statesmen and historical figures, seldom in everyday speech. 匡 means 'to correct', not 'a basket'.
usage.zh: 书面语，气势宏大，多用于政治家或历史人物，日常少用。“匡”意为匡正。

natural: refuse to eat the new dynasty's grain

meaning.en: To refuse to serve or live off a new regime out of loyalty to the old one or to one's principles.
meaning.zh: 不吃周朝的粮食，指坚持气节，不肯依附新朝或不合作。

equivalents: refuse to serve the new regime

examples.zh: 他以遗民自居，不食周粟，隐居山中。
examples.en: Regarding himself as a loyalist of the old order, he refused the new regime and lived in the mountains.

examples.zh: 面对高薪诱惑，她说自己做不到不食周粟，但也不会出卖原则。
examples.en: Faced with a big salary she said she could not play the Bo Yi, but would not sell her principles.

story.en: Bo Yi and Shu Qi, loyal to the fallen Shang, refused to eat Zhou grain and starved on Mount Shouyang.
story.zh: 伯夷、叔齐“义不食周粟，隐于首阳山，采薇而食之”，终饿死。

usage.en: Refers to Bo Yi and Shu Qi. Often praises integrity, but can be used jokingly for refusing a job or favour on principle. Literary.
usage.zh: 指伯夷、叔齐。多赞扬气节，也可戏用于出于原则拒绝某份工作或好处。书面语。

natural: rice as dear as pearls, firewood as dear as cassia

meaning.en: Food and fuel are extremely expensive, making life very hard.
meaning.zh: 粮食像珍珠一样贵，柴像桂木一样贵，形容物价昂贵，生活困难。

equivalents: the cost of living is crippling

examples.zh: 战乱年间米珠薪桂，百姓苦不堪言。
examples.en: In the war years food and fuel were dear beyond reach and ordinary people suffered terribly.

examples.zh: 灾后物资紧缺，一时米珠薪桂。
examples.en: After the disaster supplies were short and necessities cost a fortune.

story.en: Su Qin told the King of Chu that food at his court cost more than jade and firewood more than cassia.
story.zh: 苏秦说：“楚国之食贵于玉，薪贵于桂，谒者难得见如鬼，王难得见如天帝。”

usage.en: Describes inflation or scarcity, usually in hard times. Literary; not used for a single expensive item.
usage.zh: 形容物价飞涨、物资匮乏，多指艰难时期。书面语，不用于单件贵重物品。

natural: take up one's old trade again

meaning.en: To go back to one's old line of work or old habit after giving it up.
meaning.zh: 重操旧业，比喻放弃后又干起老行当或旧习惯。

examples.zh: 退役三年后，他再作冯妇，重返赛场。
examples.en: Three years after retiring he came out of retirement and returned to competition.

examples.zh: 他说戒了赌，可别又再作冯妇。
examples.en: He says he has quit gambling, but don't let him go back to it.

story.en: Feng Fu, once a tiger-catcher who had reformed into a gentleman, saw a crowd chasing a tiger, rolled up his sleeves and went back to it.
story.zh: 晋人有冯妇者，善搏虎，卒为善士；则之野，有众逐虎……冯妇攘臂下车。

usage.en: The tone depends on context: neutral for a comeback, mildly negative for relapse into a bad habit. Literary; 冯妇 is a person, read féng.
usage.zh: 视语境而定：复出时中性，旧习复发时略带贬义。书面语。“冯妇”是人名，读 féng。

natural: a great debt of gratitude

meaning.en: Great kindness and favour done for someone, for which they owe deep gratitude.
meaning.zh: 极大的恩惠和恩情。

equivalents: a debt that can never be repaid

examples.zh: 您的大恩大德，我们全家永世不忘。
examples.en: Our whole family will never forget your great kindness.

examples.zh: 老师的大恩大德，学生无以为报。
examples.en: I can never repay my teacher for such great kindness.

usage.en: Used about the benefactor's act, usually in expressions of thanks: 您的大恩大德. Neutral to formal; the phrase is often exaggerated in speech.
usage.zh: 指施恩者的恩情，常在致谢时说“您的大恩大德”。中性偏正式，口语中常带夸张。

natural: feeding the lord a half-eaten peach

meaning.en: Allusion to favour that turns to hatred: what once won praise later brings punishment when the ruler's affection fades.
meaning.zh: 弥子瑕把吃剩的桃子给卫君吃，起初被称赞，后来失宠反成罪状，比喻爱憎无常，得宠时的行为失宠后成罪过。

equivalents: what pleased the master now offends

examples.zh: 伴君如伴虎，余桃啖君的故事不是笑话。
examples.en: Serving a ruler is like keeping company with a tiger, and the story of the half-eaten peach is no joke.

examples.zh: 他得宠时的小过也被夸，失宠后便成了余桃啖君的下场。
examples.en: Minor faults were praised while he was in favour; once out of favour he met the fate of the half-eaten peach.

story.en: Mi Zixu gave Duke Ling of Wei a half-eaten peach and was praised for his devotion; once he lost favour, the same act was called an insult.
story.zh: 弥子瑕“啗君以余桃”，及色衰爱弛，得罪于君，君曰：“是尝啖我以余桃。”

date.en: end of Warring States, 3rd c. BC

usage.en: A cautionary allusion about the fickleness of rulers or bosses. Rare and literary; 余 here means 'left over'. Also related to 断袖.
usage.zh: 警示君主或上司爱憎无常。罕见，书面语；“余”指剩下的。

natural: Kong Rong giving up the big pears

meaning.en: Allusion to a child who modestly takes the smallest pear and gives the best to his elders and siblings; a model of courtesy and brotherly respect.
meaning.zh: 孔融四岁时让大梨给兄长，比喻从小懂礼貌、谦让友爱。

equivalents: taking the smallest pear for others

examples.zh: 三岁的妹妹也学会了孔融让梨，把大苹果让给哥哥。
examples.en: Even three-year-old sister has learned to share like Kong Rong, giving the bigger apple to her brother.

examples.zh: 爸爸常给孩子讲孔融让梨的故事。
examples.en: Dad often tells the children the story of Kong Rong and the pears.

origin.source: 《后汉书·孔融传》李贤注引《融家传》

story.en: At four, Kong Rong was given pears and took only the smallest, saying he was the youngest and should take the small one.
story.zh: 融年四岁，每与诸兄共食梨，融辄引小者。大人问其故，答曰：“我小儿，法当取小者。”

usage.en: A story-title allusion, used when teaching children to be modest and share. Neutral, warm; often in textbooks and parenting. Kong Rong was a Han-dynasty scholar.
usage.zh: 故事典故，常用于教育孩子谦让友爱，多见于课本和家庭教育。孔融是东汉文人。

natural: studying by firefly light and snow-glow

meaning.en: Diligent study despite poverty and poor conditions.
meaning.zh: 形容家境贫寒而刻苦读书。

equivalents: burning the midnight oil in hardship

examples.zh: 十年萤窗雪案，他终于考上了理想的学府。
examples.en: After ten years of hard study in poor conditions he finally entered his dream university.

examples.zh: 她萤窗雪案，从山村走进了大学。
examples.en: Studying through hardship, she went from a mountain village to university.

usage.en: Combines the stories of Che Yin (reading by fireflies in a bag) and Sun Kang (reading by snowlight). Literary praise of diligent students; often in graduation speeches.
usage.zh: 合用车胤囊萤、孙康映雪两个典故。书面语，称赞刻苦读书的人，常见于毕业致辞。

natural: even spit turns into pearls

meaning.en: Every word one utters is polished and valuable; praise for eloquence or fine writing.
meaning.zh: 随口说出的话都成为珠玉，形容言辞或文章极其精彩。

examples.zh: 他出口成章，咳唾成珠，令满座叹服。
examples.en: Every sentence he spoke was a gem, and the whole room was amazed.

examples.zh: 这位散文家笔下咳唾成珠，篇篇可诵。
examples.en: This essayist writes pearls, and every piece is worth reciting.

usage.en: Hyperbolic praise of speech or writing; literary and a bit old-fashioned. Not for ordinary good speaking.
usage.zh: 对言谈或文章的夸张赞美，书面语，略显古雅，不用于一般的“说得好”。

natural: a grain of millet in a great granary

meaning.en: Something tiny and insignificant in comparison with the whole.
meaning.zh: 大粮仓里的一粒小米，比喻极其渺小、微不足道。

equivalents: a grain of sand on the beach

examples.zh: 这笔捐款对灾区来说不过是太仓一粟。
examples.en: This donation is only a drop in the ocean for the disaster area.

examples.zh: 个人的力量在历史长河中只是太仓一粟。
examples.en: Individual strength is a drop in the ocean of history.

usage.en: Stresses smallness against a huge whole, either modestly or critically. Literary; 沧海一粟 is a common near-synonym.
usage.zh: 强调相对于整体极其渺小，可作自谦或批评。书面语，近义词“沧海一粟”更常见。

natural: repay with a gushing spring

meaning.en: To repay a small kindness with great generosity.
meaning.zh: 受人一点恩惠，要以加倍的方式回报。

equivalents: repay a kindness many times over

examples.zh: 当年你帮了我，今日我必当涌泉相报。
examples.en: You helped me then, and I will repay you many times over.

examples.zh: 滴水之恩，当涌泉相报。
examples.en: A drop of kindness should be repaid with a gushing spring.

usage.en: Usually in the saying 滴水之恩，当涌泉相报. Warm, formal-to-neutral; said about repaying benefactors, not about favours one does.
usage.zh: 常见于“滴水之恩，当涌泉相报”。语气温暖，中性偏正式，用于回报恩人。

natural: praise or blame in a single word

meaning.en: Passing clear judgement through the choice of a single word, as in the 'Spring and Autumn Annals' style.
meaning.zh: 用一个字表示褒贬，形容用词精当、寓意深刻。

examples.zh: 史家用笔，往往一字褒贬。
examples.en: Historians pass judgement through a single word.

examples.zh: 这段评论一字褒贬，分寸拿捏得很准。
examples.en: In this commentary each word carries praise or blame with precise judgement.

usage.en: Refers to 春秋笔法, the Confucian tradition of moral judgement through wording. Also used of exacting critics. Literary.
usage.zh: 指“春秋笔法”，即以用字表达褒贬。也用于称赞或指出评论者措辞严谨。书面语。

natural: a single word that ruins a state

meaning.en: A single ill-judged statement by a ruler can ruin a country.
meaning.zh: 一句话可以使国家灭亡，指一句错误的话可造成严重后果。

equivalents: one word can bring down a nation
a single rash remark can be disastrous

examples.zh: 领导者一言丧邦，不可不慎。
examples.en: A leader's single careless word can be fatal, so be careful.

examples.zh: 这个错误指令险些一言丧邦。
examples.en: That wrong order came close to being one word that ruined everything.

story.en: Duke Ding asked whether one saying could ruin a state; Confucius said such certainty is not possible, but there is the saying 'I take no pleasure in being ruler, except that nobody opposes my words'.
story.zh: 定公问：“一言而丧邦，有诸？”孔子对曰：“言不可以若是其几也。”

usage.en: Warns against careless words from the powerful. Usually paired with 一言兴邦 ('one word can make a state flourish'). Literary and serious.
usage.zh: 警示居上位者慎言。常与“一言兴邦”并提。书面语，语气严肃。

natural: petty craft of insect-carving and seal-cutting

meaning.en: Minor literary craftsmanship; a modest way to call one's own writing a trivial skill.
meaning.zh: 指微不足道的小技，多比喻只讲辞藻的小文章，常作自谦。

examples.zh: 我这点文字不过是雕虫篆刻，不足挂齿。
examples.en: My writing is only trivial word-craft, nothing worth mentioning.

examples.zh: 他认为写诗是雕虫篆刻，不如做些实事。
examples.en: He thought poetry a trivial pastime, and preferred to do something practical.

story.en: Yang Xiong recalled that in youth he liked writing fu, then said: 'a child's insect-carving and seal-script; a grown man would not do it' (壮夫不为也).
story.zh: 扬雄《法言》：“或问：‘吾子少而好赋？’曰：‘然。童子雕虫篆刻。’俄而曰：‘壮夫不为也。’”

date.zh: 西汉末至新 · 前1世纪—1世纪
date.en: late Western Han to Xin, 1st c. BC–1st c. AD

usage.en: Often self-deprecating about one's own writing; said of others it is dismissive. Often shortened to 雕虫小技. Literary.
usage.zh: 常自谦文笔，用于他人则含轻视。常缩为“雕虫小技”。书面语。

natural: Wei Sheng clinging to the bridge pillar

meaning.en: Absolute fidelity to a promise, even at the cost of one's life; also stubborn rigidity.
meaning.zh: 尾生为守约定，抱着桥柱被水淹死，形容坚守信约，也讽刺过于迂腐。

equivalents: keeping a promise to the death
foolish rigidity in keeping one's word

examples.zh: 他尾生抱柱般死守承诺，哪怕公司已经破产。
examples.en: He clung to his promise to the very end, though the company had gone bankrupt.

examples.zh: 守信是对的，但不必尾生抱柱。
examples.en: Keeping your word is right, but there is no need to cling to it like Wei Sheng.

story.en: Wei Sheng arranged to meet a woman under a bridge; the water rose, and he clung to the pillar and drowned rather than leave.
story.zh: 尾生与女子期于梁下，女子不来，水至不去，抱梁柱而死。

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

usage.en: A two-edged allusion: admiring faithfulness or mocking blind rigidity. Context decides. Also a lover's constancy in some stories. Literary.
usage.zh: 双面典故：既可赞守信，又可讽迂腐，视语境而定。也有用于形容情侣忠贞。书面语。

natural: feel like old friends at the first meeting

meaning.en: To become close at first meeting, as if one had always been friends.
meaning.zh: 路上相遇，停车交谈，一见如故，形容初次相识就十分投机。

equivalents: hit it off at first sight

examples.zh: 我们素不相识，却倾盖如故，聊了一晚。
examples.en: We were strangers, yet clicked like old friends and talked all night.

examples.zh: 两位学者初次见面便倾盖如故。
examples.en: The two scholars hit it off at their first meeting.

story.en: Zou Yang quoted the proverb: 'Some are white-haired yet still like new acquaintances; some meet by the roadside, canopies tilted, and are like old friends.'
story.zh: 谚曰：“有白头如新，倾盖如故。”

usage.en: Fondness at first meeting; literary, near-synonym of 一见如故 (which is more common). Often paired with 白头如新.
usage.zh: 形容初见投缘；书面语，近义词“一见如故”更常用。常与“白头如新”对举。

literal: have · will · in the end · succeed
natural: where there's a will there's a way

meaning.en: A person with firm resolve will eventually achieve the goal.
meaning.zh: 有志向、有毅力的人，终究能成功。

equivalents: where there's a will, there's a way
determination wins out in the end

examples.zh: 他苦练十年，终于夺冠，真是有志竟成。
examples.en: After ten years of hard training he finally won the title: where there's a will there's a way.

examples.zh: 有志竟成，别轻易放弃梦想。
examples.en: Where there's a will there's a way, so don't give up your dreams easily.

story.en: Emperor Guangwu praised Geng Yan for conquering Qi as he had once vowed: 'He who has the will, in the end, succeeds' (有志者事竟成也).
story.zh: 光武帝对耿弇说：“将军前在南阳建此大策……有志者事竟成也。”

usage.en: Encouragement; commonly stands alone as a motto, also in the pair 有志者事竟成. Neutral and uplifting.
usage.zh: 鼓励语，常单独作格言，也说“有志者事竟成”。中性，励志。

natural: arrow buried to the fletching in a rock

meaning.en: Extraordinary strength and archery skill; an arrow that pierces stone up to its feathers.
meaning.zh: 箭射入石头，连箭尾羽毛都没入，形容力量极大，箭术高超。

examples.zh: 他拉弓如满月，射石饮羽，众人叹服。
examples.en: He drew the bow to a full moon and sent an arrow deep into the rock, to everyone's awe.

examples.zh: 传说中的神射手个个射石饮羽。
examples.en: The legendary marksmen were all said to bury arrows in stone.

story.en: The archer Yang You-ji shot at what he took for a rhinoceros; it was a rock, and his arrow sank in up to the feathers.
story.zh: 养由基射兕中石，矢乃饮羽，诚乎兕也。

usage.en: Hyperbole about archers or extraordinary power; also said of devoted effort that can achieve the seemingly impossible. Literary.
usage.zh: 夸张地形容射手或力量神奇；也比喻专心致志能成就看似不可能的事。书面语。

natural: jaw and cheek depending on each other

meaning.en: Two parties are so closely bound that one's fall endangers the other.
meaning.zh: 面颊和牙床骨相互依存，比喻关系密切，互相依靠。

equivalents: two sides of the same coin

examples.zh: 两国辅车相依，一方有难，另一方不会袖手旁观。
examples.en: The two countries are tightly interdependent, so one will not stand by when the other is in trouble.

examples.zh: 这两个产业辅车相依，缺一不可。
examples.en: The two industries depend on each other and neither can do without the other.

story.en: Gong Zhiqi warned the Duke of Yu that Yu and Guo were like jaw and cheek: 'the cheek and jaw depend on each other; with lips gone, teeth are cold'.
story.zh: 宫之奇谏虞公：“谚所谓‘辅车相依，唇亡齿寒’者，其虞、虢之谓也。”

usage.en: Typically about states or partners; often with 唇亡齿寒 (when the lips are gone the teeth are cold). 辅车 = cheekbone and jaw; 车 here reads chē.
usage.zh: 多指国家或合作双方。常与“唇亡齿寒”连用。“辅车”指颊骨和牙床，“车”读 chē。

natural: the Guizhou donkey's one trick

meaning.en: A person's limited skill, which looks impressive until it is tested and found trivial.
meaning.zh: 黔地之驴仅有的一点本领，比喻有限的本领，看似厉害，实则不足。

equivalents: a bag of tricks soon exhausted

examples.zh: 他那点黔驴之技，早被对手识破了。
examples.en: His meagre bag of tricks had long been seen through by his opponent.

examples.zh: 别怕，他不过是黔驴之技，几招就用完了。
examples.en: Don't be afraid; he's a one-trick pony and soon runs out of moves.

story.en: A donkey brought to Guizhou frightened a tiger by braying until the tiger, once it saw the donkey only kicked, ate it.
story.zh: 柳宗元《黔之驴》：“技止此耳！”因跳踉大㘎，断其喉，尽其肉。

usage.en: Mocks someone whose skills run out quickly; also 黔驴技穷 (the donkey's tricks run out). Slightly contemptuous. Literary.
usage.zh: 讽刺本领有限、很快用尽的人；也说“黔驴技穷”。带轻蔑。书面语。

natural: a white dragon disguised as a fish

meaning.en: A noble in disguise among commoners, risking danger to himself.
meaning.zh: 白龙化身为鱼，比喻地位高贵的人隐匿身份，微服出行，以致遭遇危险。

examples.zh: 皇帝白龙鱼服，到民间私访。
examples.en: The emperor went among the people in disguise.

examples.zh: 白龙鱼服，当心被人欺负。
examples.en: A dragon dressed as a fish had better beware of being bullied.

story.en: King Wu of Wu wanted to go drinking with commoners; Wu Zixu warned him that the white dragon who became a fish was shot by fisherman Yu Qie.
story.zh: 伍子胥谏吴王：“白龙下清泠之渊，化为鱼，渔者豫且射中其目。”

usage.en: Used of rulers or high officials going incognito; the danger implied is part of the warning. Literary.
usage.zh: 用于帝王或高官隐瞒身份出行，含有处境危险之意。书面语。
